title: Photosynthesis basics
text: Photosynthesis is how plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy. Plants use light, carbon dioxide, and water to produce sugars and release oxygen. It supports most food webs.

title: Fractions
text: The numerator is above the fraction bar and counts selected parts. The denominator is below and tells how many equal parts form the whole. Equivalent fractions name the same value, such as 1/2 and 2/4.

title: Earth seasons
text: Earth's axis tilts about 23.5 degrees. As Earth orbits the Sun, each hemisphere alternately tilts toward or away from it. This changes sunlight angle and daylight length. Seasons are not primarily caused by Earth's distance from the Sun.

title: Water cycle
text: The water cycle moves water among atmosphere, land, and bodies of water. Evaporation and transpiration add vapor; condensation forms clouds; precipitation returns water. Runoff, infiltration, and groundwater move it through the environment.

title: Weather and climate
text: Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere. Climate is the long-term pattern of weather in a region, typically summarized over decades.

title: Experiments
text: A controlled experiment compares a treatment group with a control group while keeping other variables consistent. Sound design, adequate sample size, and replication also matter.

title: Ecosystems
text: Producers make organic food, consumers eat organisms, and decomposers break down dead matter and waste, returning nutrients. These roles connect through food webs and nutrient cycles.

title: Formative assessment
text: Formative assessment gathers evidence of student understanding during learning so teachers can adapt instruction. Examples include exit tickets, questions, quick writes, and practice problems.
